title: Thresholded reservoir scheduler and soft-quota negotiation for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a thresholded "reservoir" scheduler for Dedicated GPU pools that enforces per-tenant throughput envelopes while allowing short burst forgiveness via soft quota negotiation. The feature will provide throughput guarantees (envelopes), an autoscaling hook that reacts to reservoir pressure, and graceful degradation rules that prefer non-critical tenants for spillover. This ticket covers runtime scheduler changes, API surface for configuring envelopes, telemetry additions, and a staged rollout with chaos and load tests.
acceptance_criteria: API: Admin/tenant config accepts 'envelope_tps', 'reservoir_ms', 'soft_negotiation' and returns effective policy via GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/<id>/policy
Runtime: Scheduler enforces per-tenant envelope such that long-run throughput matches configured envelope +/- 5% under steady-state traffic
Burst handling: Short bursts up to 'reservoir_ms' are served without eviction in 95% of cases for workloads simulated in benchmark harness
Autoscaling: Autoscaler receives a reservoir_pressure signal and can trigger +1 GPU when pressure sustained > 60% for 30s (configurable)
Telemetry: Grafana dashboard shows per-tenant reservoir_pressure, P50/P95/P99 latencies, eviction_count and GPU_util; alerts for reservoir_pressure > 80%
Rollout: Feature behind runtime feature-flag; gradual rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% of Dedicated capacity with rollback playbook validated
Compatibility: Fallback policy to existing hard-eviction paths if soft-negotiation kernel fails or when resource contention is extreme

progress_updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff design; aligned on 'envelope' as long-run TPS target and 'reservoir_ms' as burst slack. Decided to implement credits-based reservoir (millisecond-to-token conversion) to keep accounting simple across GPUs.

2026-02-20: Prototype credit allocator implemented (local simulation). Early perf shows reservoir works with synthetic token streams; observed 12% improvement in served-burst ratio vs hard-eviction baseline.

2026-03-02: Design review with Product and SRE. Product asked for per-tenant priority class; SRE requested conservative autoscale hook defaults. Action: add 'priority_class' and 'pressure_window_secs' to API model.

2026-03-09: Runtime integration: reservoir_pressure metric emitted; initial Grafana panels created. Running cluster smoke tests on staging with 50 tenants. Observed two edge cases where priority inversion occurs under mixed workloads — creating dedicated follow-up tasks.
2026-03-12: Security and infra review notes received: ensure KMS keys not required; policy changes only via admin roles. Added requirement to audit policy changes in control-plane logs.
decisions: Use soft negotiation (credit borrowing) instead of immediate hard eviction to reduce tail latency for small bursts
Autoscaler will use 'reservoir_pressure' as a first-class signal; do not autoscale on single transient spike (use sustained window)
Per-tenant 'priority_class' will determine order of graceful degradation; default mapping: critical -> 1, standard -> 5, best-effort -> 10
Expose policies via Dedicated API (not user-managed on hosted) to preserve isolation and enterprise control
tradeoffs: Soft negotiation reduces evictions and improves latency for bursty tenants but increases risk of temporary SLA violations for strict commit customers; mitigated by 'priority_class' and explicit envelope tuning
Reservoir accounting adds small CPU overhead per-request; acceptable given GPU cost savings and fewer cold autoscale events
Autoscale on reservoir_pressure trades some sensitivity (delay to trigger) for stability—may increase the window where tenants see degraded throughput during rapid growth
risks: Priority inversion under specific mixes of long-running and bursty workloads — mitigated via additional fairness check and emergency preempt policy
Incorrect envelope tuning could starve best-effort tenants for extended periods; add safety caps and eviction quotas
Telemetry gaps could make diagnosing production regressions slow; ensure we add high-cardinality sampling for top tenants
benchmarks: Target: Maintain configured envelope +/-5% throughput for steady-state; serve 95% of bursts <= reservoir_ms without eviction; reduce eviction_count by >=30% vs baseline under mixed workloads. Baseline measured on staging: eviction_rate=0.24 evictions/min, avg_GPU_util=62%.
qa_plan: Unit tests for credit accounting and edge conditions (negative credits, concurrent returns)
Integration tests with autoscaler hook and simulated sustained pressure
E2E benchmark: 500-tenants mixed traffic profile comparing baseline vs reservoir feature
Chaos test: random node failures while reservoir_policy enabled; validate rollback path triggers and no silent policy corruption
rollout_plan: Stage 1: enable on 10% of Dedicated capacity in staging - run 48h smoke + benchmark
Stage 2: enable on 10% production non-enterprise tenants - monitor key metrics 72h
Stage 3: enable on Dedicated test clusters for enterprise customers with opt-in
Stage 4: full rollout with gradual ramp and automated rollback if reservoir_pressure alerts breach thresholds
